records.literal_gloss: And spoke YHWH to Joshua, saying,

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Joshua, saying,

es.L: Y habló {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} a Josué, diciendo:

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} parla à Josué, en disant :

decisions.choice: the LORD spoke to Joshua: the command about the cities of refuge is now carried out
decisions.reason: God had given this command to Moses (Numbers 35:9-15; Deuteronomy 19:1-10). Now that the land west of the Jordan has been divided among the tribes (19:51), God tells Joshua to put it into effect.

source.text: דַּבֵּ֛ר אֶל־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר תְּנ֤וּ לָכֶם֙ אֶת־עָרֵ֣י הַמִּקְלָ֔ט אֲשֶׁר־דִּבַּ֥רְתִּי אֲלֵיכֶ֖ם בְּיַד־מֹשֶֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: Speak to [the] sons of Israel, saying, give for yourselves the cities of the refuge which I spoke to you by [the] hand of Moses,

en.L: "Speak to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, saying, 'Assign for yourselves the cities of refuge of which I spoke to you by the hand of Moses,
en.B: "Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}: 'Appoint the cities of refuge that I told you about through Moses,
en.R: "Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}: 'Choose the towns of safety that I told you about through Moses.

sw.L: "Sema na wana wa Israeli, ukisema, 'Jiwekeeni miji ya makimbilio ambayo niliwaambia habari zake kwa mkono wa Musa,
sw.B: "Waambie Waisraeli: 'Tengeni miji ya makimbilio niliyowaambia habari zake kupitia Musa,
sw.R: "Waambie Waisraeli: 'Chagueni miji ya makimbilio, mahali ambapo mtu anaweza kukimbilia awe salama, kama nilivyowaambia kupitia Musa.

es.L: «Habla a los hijos de Israel, diciendo: “{{plural_you:Señalen|Señalad}} para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} las ciudades de refugio de las que {{plural_you:les|os}} hablé por mano de Moisés,
es.B: «Di a los israelitas: “{{plural_you:Designen|Designad}} las ciudades de refugio de las que {{plural_you:les|os}} hablé por medio de Moisés,
es.R: «Diles a los israelitas: “{{plural_you:Escojan|Escoged}} los pueblos de refugio de los que {{plural_you:les|os}} hablé por medio de Moisés.

fr.L: « Parle aux {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël, en disant : “Donnez-vous les villes de refuge dont je vous ai parlé par la main de Moïse,
fr.B: « Dis aux {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} : “Désignez les villes de refuge dont je vous ai parlé par l’intermédiaire de Moïse,
fr.R: « Dis aux {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} : “Choisissez les villes de refuge dont je vous ai parlé par l’intermédiaire de Moïse.

vi.L: "Hãy nói với con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên rằng: 'Hãy định cho các ngươi các thành ẩn náu mà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã phán với các ngươi qua tay Môi-se,
vi.B: "Con hãy bảo dân Y-sơ-ra-ên: 'Hãy chỉ định các thành ẩn náu mà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã phán với các ngươi qua Môi-se,
vi.R: "Con hãy bảo dân Y-sơ-ra-ên: 'Hãy chọn các thành ẩn náu mà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nói với các ngươi qua Môi-se.

ko.L: "이스라엘 자손에게 말하여라. '내가 모세를 통하여 너희에게 말한 도피성들을 너희를 위하여 정하여,
ko.B: "이스라엘 자손에게 말하여라. '내가 모세를 통하여 너희에게 일러 준 도피성들을 정하여라.
ko.R: "이스라엘 백성에게 말하여라. '내가 모세를 통하여 너희에게 말한, 피할 성읍들을 정하여라.

decisions.choice: cities of refuge: towns where a person who had killed someone could find protection
decisions.reason: The word for refuge means a place where someone is taken in and sheltered. These towns protected a killer from revenge until the case was judged (verses 3, 6; Numbers 35:11-12).

decisions.choice: which I spoke to you through Moses: the laws of Numbers 35 and Deuteronomy 19
decisions.reason: God refers to what Moses had already taught: six cities, three on each side of the Jordan (Numbers 35:9-34), with the rules for who may flee there (Deuteronomy 19:1-13). Moses had already named the three cities east of the Jordan (Deuteronomy 4:41-43).

decisions.choice: by the hand of Moses: through Moses
decisions.reason: "By the hand of" names the person through whom something is done or said; Moses was the one who passed God's words on.

decisions.choice: cities of refuge (Literal, Balanced) / towns of safety (Readable)
decisions.reason: The same terms as in Numbers 35 and Deuteronomy 19. Readable says "towns of safety" so the purpose of the towns is plain.

decisions.choice: single quotation marks for the words to Israel
decisions.reason: God's words to Joshua open with a double quotation mark; the message Joshua is to give the people opens with a single one here, and both close at the end of verse 6. Literal and Balanced end the verse with a comma because the sentence runs on into verse 3.

decisions.choice: "miji ya makimbilio" at every level; Readable adds "mahali ambapo mtu anaweza kukimbilia awe salama"
decisions.reason: The term fixed for these books: "makimbilio" is a place one runs to for safety. The English Readable says "towns of safety"; Swahili keeps the term at Readable too and explains it once, where it first appears.

decisions.choice: "las ciudades de refugio" (L, B); "los pueblos de refugio" (R)
decisions.reason: As the terms note sets: "ciudades de refugio". Readable says "pueblos", as it does for towns throughout, and keeps "refugio", a plain everyday word for a safe place, where the English Readable says "towns of safety". The words to Israel stand inside the LORD's words, so they take the inner Spanish quotation marks “ ”.

decisions.choice: "les villes de refuge" at every level
decisions.reason: The block's terms note sets "villes de refuge". The phrase is already plain French, a town where one takes refuge, so Readable keeps it where the English Readable says "towns of safety".

decisions.choice: the LORD's words to Israel in “ ” inside Joshua's « »
decisions.reason: French marks a quotation inside a quotation with “ ”, as the style guide sets, where the English uses single quotation marks.

decisions.choice: "도피성" (L, B); "피할 성읍" (R) for the cities of refuge
decisions.reason: The terms note sets "도피성". Readable says the same thing in plain native words, as the English Readable says "towns of safety". The words to Israel take single quotation marks inside the LORD's speech, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "các thành ẩn náu" at every level
decisions.reason: As the terms note for Joshua sets; "ẩn náu" is plain enough for Readable too, so the English Readable "towns of safety" needs no separate word.

decisions.choice: The LORD speaks of Israel as "các ngươi" at every level; Joshua himself is "con" (B, R)
decisions.reason: God's words to Israel as a nation keep "các ngươi" at every level, as his laws do in the Pentateuch; "con" is for Joshua, his servant (1:2).

source.text: לָנ֥וּס שָׁ֨מָּה֙ רוֹצֵ֔חַ מַכֵּה־נֶ֥פֶשׁ בִּשְׁגָגָ֖ה בִּבְלִי־דָ֑עַת וְהָי֤וּ לָכֶם֙ לְמִקְלָ֔ט מִגֹּאֵ֖ל הַדָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: to flee there [a] killer, striking [a] person by inadvertence, without knowledge; and they will be for you for refuge from [the] avenger of the blood.

en.L: so that a killer who strikes a person by mistake, without knowing, may flee there; and they shall be for you a refuge from the avenger of blood.
en.B: so that anyone who kills a person by mistake, without meaning to, can flee there. They will be a place of refuge for you from the avenger of blood.
en.R: Anyone who kills a person by accident, without meaning to, can run away to one of these towns. The towns will protect you from the relative who avenges the death.

sw.L: ili mwuaji amwuaye mtu kwa makosa, bila kujua, akimbilie huko; nayo itakuwa kwenu makimbilio kutokana na mlipiza kisasi wa damu.
sw.B: ili mtu yeyote amwuaye mtu kwa makosa, bila kukusudia, aweze kukimbilia huko. Miji hiyo itakuwa mahali pa makimbilio kwenu kutokana na mlipiza kisasi wa damu.
sw.R: Mtu yeyote atakayemwua mtu kwa bahati mbaya, bila kukusudia, anaweza kukimbilia mmojawapo wa miji hiyo. Miji hiyo itawalinda dhidi ya ndugu wa marehemu anayetaka kulipiza kisasi cha kifo chake.

es.L: para que huya allí el homicida que hiera a una persona por error, sin saber[lo]; y {{plural_you:les|os}} servirán de refugio contra el vengador de la sangre.
es.B: para que cualquiera que mate a una persona por error, sin querer, pueda huir allí. Serán para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} un lugar de refugio contra el vengador de la sangre.
es.R: Cualquiera que mate a una persona por accidente, sin querer, podrá huir a uno de esos pueblos. Los pueblos {{plural_you:los|os}} protegerán del pariente que venga la muerte.

fr.L: pour que s’y enfuie le meurtrier qui frappe une personne par erreur, sans le savoir ; et elles seront pour vous un refuge contre le vengeur du sang.
fr.B: afin que celui qui a tué une personne par erreur, sans le vouloir, puisse s’y réfugier. Elles vous serviront de refuge contre le vengeur du sang.
fr.R: Celui qui a tué quelqu’un par accident, sans le vouloir, pourra s’enfuir dans l’une de ces villes. Elles vous protégeront contre le parent qui venge le mort.

vi.L: để kẻ sát nhân lỡ tay đánh chết một người, không biết, có thể trốn đến đó; và các thành ấy sẽ là nơi ẩn náu cho các ngươi khỏi người báo thù máu.
vi.B: để bất cứ ai lỡ tay giết người, không cố ý, có thể trốn đến đó. Các thành ấy sẽ là nơi ẩn náu cho các ngươi khỏi người báo thù máu.
vi.R: Ai vô tình giết người, không cố ý, có thể chạy trốn đến một trong các thành ấy. Các thành ấy sẽ bảo vệ các ngươi khỏi người bà con muốn báo thù cho người chết.

ko.L: 실수로, 알지 못하고 사람을 친 살인자가 그리로 도망하게 하여라. 그리고 그것들이 너희에게 피의 보복자에게서 피할 곳이 될 것이다.
ko.B: 실수로, 뜻하지 않게 사람을 죽인 사람이 그리로 도망할 수 있게 하여라. 그 성읍들은 너희에게 피의 보복자를 피할 곳이 될 것이다.
ko.R: 누구든지 실수로, 죽일 뜻이 없이 사람을 죽였으면 이 성읍들 가운데 하나로 도망할 수 있다. 이 성읍들은 죽은 사람의 원수를 갚으려는 친척에게서 너희를 지켜 줄 것이다.

decisions.choice: killer: anyone who has caused another person's death
decisions.reason: The word names one who has killed someone, whether on purpose or not. In this law it means the one who killed by accident and now needs protection (Numbers 35:11).

decisions.choice: by mistake, without knowledge: without intending it
decisions.reason: The first phrase is the one used in Numbers 35:11, 15 and for unintentional sins (Leviticus 4:2); the second is the one used in Deuteronomy 4:42 and 19:4. Together they stress that the killing was not planned or wanted.

decisions.choice: the avenger of blood: the dead person's close relative, whose duty was to avenge the death
decisions.reason: The word for avenger is the same word as the family redeemer, the relative bound to stand up for the family. Here his duty was to put a murderer to death (Numbers 35:19, 21). The cities protected someone who had killed by accident from him.

decisions.choice: without knowledge: kept, as in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The oldest Greek translation of Joshua appears to lack this phrase here, as it lacks most of verses 4-6 (see the notes there). This description comes from general knowledge of the manuscripts and must be checked against a Greek apparatus by a reviewer.

decisions.choice: anyone who kills a person
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly what the striking was: a blow that killed, as in Numbers 35:11. The words are already inclusive. Readable begins a new sentence and adds "one of these towns" so it is clear where the person runs.

decisions.choice: the relative who avenges the death
decisions.reason: Readable explains who the avenger of blood was, as in Numbers 35 and Deuteronomy 19.

decisions.choice: "ndugu wa marehemu anayetaka kulipiza kisasi" (the dead person's relative who seeks to avenge)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "mlipiza kisasi wa damu" (the avenger of blood). Readable says who he was, a close relative of the one who died, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "el vengador de la sangre" (L, B); "el pariente que venga la muerte" (R)
decisions.reason: The avenger of blood was the dead person's nearest male relative, whose duty was to take a life for a life (Numbers 35:19). Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew title; Readable says who he was, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "le vengeur du sang" (L, B), "le parent qui venge le mort" (R)
decisions.reason: The goel of blood was the dead person's close relative, whose duty was to avenge the death. Literal and Balanced keep the traditional phrase; Readable says who he was, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "피의 보복자" (L, B); "죽은 사람의 원수를 갚으려는 친척" (R)
decisions.reason: The avenger of blood was the dead person's close relative, whose duty was to avenge the death (meaning decision m3). Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew title; Readable says who he was, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "người báo thù máu" (Literal, Balanced); "người bà con muốn báo thù cho người chết" (Readable)
decisions.reason: The avenger of blood is the dead person's close relative (meaning decision); Readable says who he is, as the English does. "máu", not "huyết", is the word for blood settled in the Pentateuch.

source.text: וְנָ֞ס אֶל־אַחַ֣ת׀מֵהֶעָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֗לֶּה וְעָמַד֙ פֶּ֚תַח שַׁ֣עַר הָעִ֔יר וְדִבֶּ֛ר בְּאָזְנֵ֛י זִקְנֵ֥י־הָעִֽירהַהִ֖יא אֶת־דְּבָרָ֑יו וְאָסְפ֨וּ אֹת֤וֹ הָעִ֨ירָה֙ אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם וְנָתְנוּ־ל֥וֹ מָק֖וֹם וְיָשַׁ֥ב עִמָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will flee to one of the cities the these, and he will stand [at the] entrance of [the] gate of the city, and he will speak in [the] ears of [the] elders of the city the that his words; and they will gather him into the city to them, and they will give to him [a] place, and he will live with them.

en.L: And he shall flee to one of these cities, and stand at the entrance of the gate of the city, and speak his words in the ears of the elders of that city; and they shall take him into the city to themselves and give him a place, and he shall live with them.
en.B: The one who killed is to flee to one of these cities, stand at the entrance of the city gate and explain the case to the elders of that city. Then they are to take {{gender:that person|him}} into the city and give {{gender:them|him}} a place to live among them.
en.R: That person must run to one of these towns and stand at the entrance of the town gate. There {{gender:they|he}} must tell the elders of the town what happened. Then the elders must take {{gender:them|him}} into the town and give {{gender:them|him}} a place to live with them.

sw.L: Naye atakimbilia mmojawapo wa miji hii, na kusimama mahali pa kuingilia lango la mji, na kusema maneno yake masikioni mwa wazee wa mji ule; nao watamkaribisha ndani ya mji kwao, na kumpa mahali, naye atakaa pamoja nao.
sw.B: Mtu aliyeua atakimbilia mmojawapo wa miji hiyo, asimame mahali pa kuingilia lango la mji, na kuwaeleza wazee wa mji ule jambo lake. Kisha watamkaribisha ndani ya mji na kumpa mahali pa kuishi kati yao.
sw.R: Mtu huyo lazima akimbilie mmojawapo wa miji hiyo na kusimama mahali pa kuingilia lango la mji. Huko lazima awaeleze wazee wa mji yaliyotokea. Kisha wazee lazima wamkaribishe ndani ya mji na kumpa mahali pa kuishi pamoja nao.

es.L: Y huirá a una de estas ciudades, y se presentará a la entrada de la puerta de la ciudad, y expondrá su caso a oídos de los ancianos de aquella ciudad; y ellos lo recibirán en la ciudad consigo, y le darán un lugar, y habitará con ellos.
es.B: Quien haya matado huirá a una de estas ciudades, se presentará a la entrada de la puerta de la ciudad y explicará su caso a los ancianos de aquella ciudad. Entonces ellos recibirán a esa persona en la ciudad y le darán un lugar donde vivir entre ellos.
es.R: Esa persona tiene que huir a uno de esos pueblos y presentarse a la entrada de la puerta del pueblo. Allí tiene que contarles a los ancianos del pueblo lo que pasó. Entonces los ancianos tienen que recibirla en el pueblo y darle un lugar donde vivir con ellos.

fr.L: Et il s’enfuira vers l’une de ces villes, et se tiendra à l’entrée de la porte de la ville, et dira ses paroles aux oreilles des anciens de cette ville ; et ils le recueilleront dans la ville auprès d’eux, et lui donneront un lieu, et il habitera avec eux.
fr.B: Celui qui a tué s’enfuira dans l’une de ces villes, se tiendra à l’entrée de la porte de la ville et exposera son cas aux anciens de cette ville. Alors ils l’accueilleront dans la ville et lui donneront un endroit où habiter parmi eux.
fr.R: Cette personne devra courir jusqu’à l’une de ces villes et se tenir à l’entrée de la porte de la ville. Là, elle racontera aux anciens de la ville ce qui s’est passé. Ensuite, les anciens devront l’accueillir dans la ville et lui donner un endroit où vivre avec eux.

vi.L: Người ấy sẽ trốn đến một trong các thành này, đứng tại lối vào cổng thành, và trình bày sự việc của mình vào tai các trưởng lão thành ấy; họ sẽ đem người ấy vào thành với họ, cho người ấy một chỗ, và người ấy sẽ ở với họ.
vi.B: Người đã giết người phải trốn đến một trong các thành này, đứng tại lối vào cổng thành và trình bày sự việc với các trưởng lão của thành. Rồi họ phải đem người ấy vào thành và cho người ấy một chỗ ở giữa họ.
vi.R: Người ấy phải chạy đến một trong các thành này và đứng tại lối vào cổng thành. Ở đó người ấy phải kể cho các trưởng lão của thành biết điều đã xảy ra. Rồi các trưởng lão phải đem người ấy vào thành và cho người ấy một chỗ để sống với họ.

ko.L: 그리고 그는 이 성읍들 가운데 하나로 도망하여 그 성읍 문 어귀에 서서, 그 성읍 장로들의 귀에 자기 말을 할 것이다. 그러면 그들이 그를 성읍 안으로 자기들에게 받아들이고 그에게 곳을 주어, 그가 그들과 함께 살 것이다.
ko.B: 사람을 죽인 그 사람은 이 성읍들 가운데 하나로 도망하여 성문 어귀에 서서, 그 성읍 장로들에게 자기 사정을 말해야 한다. 그러면 장로들은 그 사람을 성 안으로 받아들이고, 자기들 가운데 살 곳을 마련해 주어야 한다.
ko.R: 그 사람은 이 성읍들 가운데 하나로 도망하여 성문 입구에 서야 한다. 그리고 거기에서 그 성읍의 장로들에게 무슨 일이 있었는지 말해야 한다. 그러면 장로들은 그 사람을 성 안으로 받아들이고, 자기들과 함께 살 곳을 마련해 주어야 한다.

decisions.choice: verses 4-5: kept, as in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The oldest Greek translation of Joshua, in its main manuscripts, does not have verses 4 and 5, and its verse 6 is shorter (see verse 6). The added material in the Hebrew uses the wording of Deuteronomy 19:4-6, while the shorter text follows Numbers 35. The Hebrew text is translated here. This description comes from general knowledge of the manuscripts and must be checked against a Greek apparatus by a reviewer.

decisions.choice: the entrance of the city gate: the place where the elders heard cases
decisions.reason: In Israel's towns the elders sat at the gate to settle disputes and hear legal cases (Deuteronomy 21:19; 22:15; Ruth 4:1-2). The killer comes there first, before entering the town.

decisions.choice: speak his words in the ears of: tell his case so that they hear it
decisions.reason: To speak "in the ears" of someone is to address them directly. "His words" here are his account of what happened, his side of the case.

decisions.choice: gather him into the city: take him in, give him shelter
decisions.reason: The verb means to gather; used of a person, it means to take someone in as a guest or under protection (Judges 19:15, 18).

decisions.choice: gender setting for the killer
decisions.reason: The law is written with masculine words but covers anyone who killed by accident, as in Numbers 35. Balanced and Readable use the gender setting for the pronouns; Literal keeps the masculine words.

decisions.choice: no gender spans for the one who killed
decisions.reason: The English uses the gender setting for the person who killed ("that person" or "him", "they" or "he"). Swahili pronouns and verb prefixes are the same for a man and a woman ("atakimbilia", "mtu huyo", "yeye"), so Swahili already says "that person" and has nothing for the setting to change in verses 4-9.

decisions.choice: "quien", "esa persona", "recibirla", "le" with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span with "a esa persona" and "a ese hombre"
decisions.reason: The English puts the pronouns for the killer under the gender setting, since a woman could also be the one who killed. Balanced and Readable say "quien" and "esa persona", which already take in both, and Spanish "le" has no gender, so there is no second wording for the setting to change. Literal follows the Hebrew masculine, as the English Literal does.

decisions.choice: no gender setting for the killer: "celui qui a tué ... l'accueilleront" (B), "cette personne ... elle" (R)
decisions.reason: The English uses a gender setting for the pronouns that refer to the killer. In French "celui qui" already means anyone, and the "il", "le" that refer back to it are ordinary generic French, as the style guide sets; Readable's "cette personne ... elle" follows the noun's grammar. So no span is needed.

decisions.choice: "người ấy" for the killer, with no gender span
decisions.reason: "người ấy" already means "that person" without saying man or woman, so the English choice between "they" and "he" has no Vietnamese counterpart.

decisions.choice: "그 사람" with no gender span for the one who killed
decisions.reason: The English Balanced and Readable put the pronouns for the killer under the gender setting. Korean names the person "그 사람" or "사람을 죽인 사람", which takes in men and women alike, so the setting has nothing to change. The same holds through verse 9.

source.text: וְכִ֨י יִרְדֹּ֜ף גֹּאֵ֤ל הַדָּם֙ אַֽחֲרָ֔יו וְלֹֽא־יַסְגִּ֥רוּ אֶת־הָרֹצֵ֖חַ בְּיָד֑וֹ כִּ֤י בִבְלִי־דַ֨עַת֙ הִכָּ֣ה אֶת־רֵעֵ֔הוּ וְלֹֽא־שֹׂנֵ֥א ה֛וּא ל֖וֹ מִתְּמ֥וֹל שִׁלְשֽׁוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: And if pursues [the] avenger of the blood after him, and not they will deliver the killer into his hand, because without knowledge he struck his neighbor, and not hating he [was] him from yesterday [and the] third day.

en.L: And if the avenger of blood pursues him, they shall not hand over the killer into his hand, because he struck his neighbor without knowing, and he was not hating him in time past.
en.B: If the avenger of blood comes after {{gender:them|him}}, the elders must not hand the killer over to the avenger, because the killer struck the neighbor without meaning to and had not been that neighbor's enemy before.
en.R: If the relative who avenges the death chases after {{gender:them|him}}, the elders must not hand the killer over. The killer did not mean to kill the other person and had not hated that person before.

sw.L: Na kama mlipiza kisasi wa damu akimfuatia, hawatamtia mwuaji mkononi mwake, kwa sababu alimpiga jirani yake bila kujua, wala hakuwa akimchukia tangu zamani.
sw.B: Ikiwa mlipiza kisasi wa damu atamfuatia, wazee hawapaswi kumtia mwuaji mikononi mwake, kwa sababu alimpiga jirani yake bila kukusudia, wala hakuwa adui yake hapo kabla.
sw.R: Ikiwa ndugu anayelipiza kisasi cha kifo atamfuatia, wazee hawapaswi kumkabidhi mtu huyo aliyeua. Yeye hakukusudia kumwua mwenzake, wala hakuwa amemchukia hapo kabla.

es.L: Y si el vengador de la sangre lo persigue, no entregarán al homicida en su mano, porque hirió a su prójimo sin saber[lo], y no lo odiaba desde antes.
es.B: Si el vengador de la sangre va tras esa persona, los ancianos no deben entregarle al homicida, porque mató a su prójimo sin querer y no había sido antes su enemigo.
es.R: Si el pariente que venga la muerte persigue a esa persona, los ancianos no deben entregarla. No quiso matar a la otra persona, y antes no la odiaba.

fr.L: Et si le vengeur du sang le poursuit, ils ne livreront pas le meurtrier entre ses mains, car c’est sans le savoir qu’il a frappé son prochain, et il ne le haïssait pas auparavant.
fr.B: Si le vengeur du sang le poursuit, les anciens ne devront pas lui livrer le meurtrier, car celui-ci a frappé son prochain sans le vouloir et n’était pas son ennemi auparavant.
fr.R: Si le parent qui venge le mort le poursuit, les anciens ne devront pas lui livrer le meurtrier. Celui-ci n’a pas voulu tuer l’autre personne, et il ne la détestait pas avant.

vi.L: Nếu người báo thù máu đuổi theo người ấy, họ không được nộp kẻ sát nhân vào tay hắn, vì người ấy đã đánh người lân cận mình mà không biết, và trước đây không hề ghét người lân cận ấy.
vi.B: Nếu người báo thù máu đuổi theo người ấy, các trưởng lão không được nộp kẻ sát nhân cho người báo thù, vì kẻ sát nhân đã đánh người lân cận mình mà không cố ý, và trước đó không hề thù ghét người ấy.
vi.R: Nếu người bà con muốn báo thù đuổi theo người ấy, các trưởng lão không được nộp kẻ đã giết người. Người ấy không cố ý giết người kia, và trước đó cũng không hề ghét người kia.

ko.L: 그리고 피의 보복자가 그를 뒤쫓아 오더라도 그들은 그 살인자를 그의 손에 넘겨주지 말 것이다. 그가 알지 못하고 자기 이웃을 쳤고, 전부터 그를 미워하지 않았기 때문이다.
ko.B: 피의 보복자가 그 사람을 뒤쫓아 오더라도 장로들은 그를 보복자에게 넘겨주어서는 안 된다. 그 사람은 뜻하지 않게 이웃을 죽였고, 전부터 그 이웃과 원수진 일도 없었기 때문이다.
ko.R: 죽은 사람의 원수를 갚으려는 친척이 그 사람을 뒤쫓아 오더라도 장로들은 그를 넘겨주어서는 안 된다. 그 사람은 죽일 뜻이 없었고, 전에 죽은 사람을 미워한 적도 없었기 때문이다.

decisions.choice: verse 5: kept, as in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: As in verse 4: the main manuscripts of the oldest Greek translation lack this verse.

decisions.choice: from yesterday and the third day: before, in time past
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "yesterday and the day before" for any time before. The killer had no past hatred for the one who died, which shows it was not murder (Deuteronomy 4:42; 19:4).

decisions.choice: his neighbor: a fellow member of the community
decisions.reason: The word means a companion or fellow, anyone a person lives and works with, as in Deuteronomy 19:4.

decisions.choice: the elders
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "they"; Balanced and Readable name the elders of verse 4 so it is clear who must not hand the killer over.

decisions.choice: "auparavant" at Literal for "from yesterday and the third day"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew idiom means "in time past". French has no matching picture, so Literal gives the meaning in one word, as the English Literal does.

source.text: וְיָשַׁ֣ב׀בָּעִ֣יר הַהִ֗יא עַד־עָמְד֞וֹ לִפְנֵ֤י הָֽעֵדָה֙ לַמִּשְׁפָּ֔ט עַד־מוֹת֙ הַכֹּהֵ֣ן הַגָּד֔וֹל אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִהְיֶ֖ה בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֑ם אָ֣ז׀יָשׁ֣וּב הָרוֹצֵ֗חַ וּבָ֤א אֶל־עִירוֹ֙ וְאֶל־בֵּית֔וֹ אֶל־הָעִ֖יר אֲשֶׁר־נָ֥ס מִשָּֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will live in the city the that until his standing before the congregation for the judgment, until [the] death of the priest the great who will be in the days the those; then will return the killer and will come to his city and to his house, to the city from which he fled.

en.L: And he shall live in that city until he stands before the congregation for judgment, until the death of the high priest who shall be in those days. Then the killer shall return and come to his own city and to his own house, to the city from which he fled.'"
en.B: The killer is to stay in that city until standing trial before the congregation, and until the death of the high priest who is serving at that time. Then the killer may go back home to {{gender:their|his}} own city and {{gender:their|his}} own house, the city {{gender:they|he}} fled from.'"
en.R: That person must stay in that town until the community has judged the case. {{gender:They|He}} must stay there until the high priest who is serving at that time dies. After that, the killer may go back home to {{gender:their|his}} own town and house, the town {{gender:they|he}} ran away from.'"

sw.L: Naye atakaa katika mji ule mpaka atakaposimama mbele ya jumuiya kwa hukumu, mpaka kifo cha kuhani mkuu atakayekuwepo siku zile. Ndipo mwuaji atarudi na kuja katika mji wake mwenyewe na nyumbani kwake mwenyewe, katika mji alioukimbia.'"
sw.B: Mwuaji atakaa katika mji ule mpaka atakaposimama mbele ya jumuiya kuhukumiwa, na mpaka kifo cha kuhani mkuu atakayekuwa akihudumu wakati huo. Ndipo mwuaji ataweza kurudi nyumbani katika mji wake mwenyewe na nyumba yake mwenyewe, mji ule alioukimbia.'"
sw.R: Mtu huyo lazima akae katika mji ule mpaka jumuiya itakapolihukumu shauri lake. Lazima akae huko mpaka kuhani mkuu atakayekuwa akihudumu wakati huo atakapokufa. Baada ya hapo, mwuaji anaweza kurudi nyumbani katika mji wake na nyumba yake, mji ule alioukimbia.'"

es.L: Y habitará en esa ciudad hasta que comparezca ante la comunidad para el juicio, hasta la muerte del sumo sacerdote que haya en aquellos días. Entonces el homicida volverá e irá a su ciudad y a su casa, a la ciudad de donde huyó”».
es.B: El homicida se quedará en esa ciudad hasta comparecer en juicio ante la comunidad, y hasta la muerte del sumo sacerdote que esté sirviendo en ese tiempo. Entonces podrá volver a su propia ciudad y a su propia casa, la ciudad de donde huyó”».
es.R: Esa persona tiene que quedarse en ese pueblo hasta que la comunidad haya juzgado el caso. Tiene que quedarse allí hasta que muera el sumo sacerdote que esté sirviendo en ese tiempo. Después podrá volver a su casa, en su propio pueblo, el pueblo de donde huyó”».

fr.L: Et il habitera dans cette ville jusqu’à ce qu’il comparaisse devant la communauté pour le jugement, jusqu’à la mort du grand prêtre qui sera [en fonction] en ces jours-là. Alors le meurtrier retournera et rentrera dans sa ville et dans sa maison, dans la ville d’où il s’est enfui.” »
fr.B: Le meurtrier restera dans cette ville jusqu’à ce qu’il comparaisse en jugement devant la communauté, et jusqu’à la mort du grand prêtre qui sera en fonction à ce moment-là. Alors il pourra retourner chez lui, dans sa ville et dans sa maison, la ville d’où il s’est enfui.” »
fr.R: Cette personne devra rester dans la ville jusqu’à ce que la communauté ait jugé son cas. Elle devra y rester jusqu’à la mort du grand prêtre qui sera en fonction à ce moment-là. Après cela, le meurtrier pourra rentrer chez lui, dans sa ville et dans sa maison, la ville d’où il s’est enfui.” »

vi.L: Người ấy sẽ ở trong thành ấy cho đến khi đứng trước hội chúng để chịu xét xử, cho đến khi thầy tế lễ thượng phẩm đương nhiệm trong những ngày ấy qua đời. Bấy giờ kẻ sát nhân sẽ trở về thành mình và nhà mình, về thành mà người ấy đã trốn khỏi.'"
vi.B: Kẻ sát nhân phải ở lại trong thành ấy cho đến khi ra trước hội chúng để chịu xét xử, và cho đến khi thầy tế lễ thượng phẩm đương nhiệm qua đời. Bấy giờ kẻ sát nhân mới được về nhà, về thành mình và nhà mình, là thành người ấy đã trốn khỏi.'"
vi.R: Người ấy phải ở lại trong thành ấy cho đến khi cộng đồng xét xử vụ việc. Người ấy phải ở đó cho đến khi thầy tế lễ thượng phẩm đang phục vụ lúc ấy qua đời. Sau đó, kẻ đã giết người mới được về nhà, về thành và nhà của mình, là thành người ấy đã chạy trốn khỏi.'"

ko.L: 그리고 그는 회중 앞에 서서 재판을 받을 때까지, 그때에 있을 대제사장이 죽을 때까지 그 성읍에서 살 것이다. 그런 뒤에 살인자는 돌아가서 자기 성읍, 자기 집, 곧 자기가 도망하여 나온 성읍으로 갈 것이다.'"
ko.B: 그 사람은 회중 앞에서 재판을 받을 때까지, 그리고 그때에 일하고 있는 대제사장이 죽을 때까지 그 성읍에서 살아야 한다. 그런 뒤에야 그는 자기가 도망하여 나온 성읍, 곧 자기 성읍과 자기 집으로 돌아갈 수 있다.'"
ko.R: 그 사람은 공동체가 그 일을 재판할 때까지 그 성읍에 머물러야 한다. 그리고 그때에 일하고 있는 대제사장이 죽을 때까지 거기에 머물러야 한다. 그 뒤에야 그 사람은 자기가 도망하여 나온 고향 성읍, 자기 집으로 돌아갈 수 있다.'"

decisions.choice: until ... until: two limits, first the trial, then the high priest's death
decisions.reason: The verse puts two time limits side by side. Numbers 35:12, 24-28 explains how they fit: the killer stays in the city until the congregation hears the case; if the killing is judged an accident, the killer goes back to the city of refuge and stays there until the high priest dies.

decisions.choice: the death of the high priest: the end of the time of refuge
decisions.reason: The killer's protection lasted as long as the high priest then serving was alive; after his death the killer could go home safely (Numbers 35:25, 28). The law does not say why this event ends the time of refuge.

decisions.choice: from "until the death of the high priest" to the end of the verse: kept, as in the Hebrew text
alternatives: end the verse at "for judgment", with the Greek
decisions.reason: The main manuscripts of the oldest Greek translation end this verse after "for judgment". As in verse 4, the longer Hebrew text is translated. This description comes from general knowledge of the manuscripts and must be checked against a Greek apparatus by a reviewer.

decisions.choice: closing quotation marks
decisions.reason: The message to Israel that began in verse 2 ends here, and so do God's words to Joshua: the single and the double quotation marks close together.

source.text: וַיַּקְדִּ֜שׁוּ אֶת־קֶ֤דֶשׁ בַּגָּלִיל֙ בְּהַ֣ר נַפְתָּלִ֔י וְאֶת־שְׁכֶ֖ם בְּהַ֣ר אֶפְרָ֑יִם וְאֶת־קִרְיַ֥ת אַרְבַּ֛ע הִ֥יא חֶבְר֖וֹן בְּהַ֥ר יְהוּדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they set apart Kedesh in Galilee in [the] hill country of Naphtali, and Shechem in [the] hill country of Ephraim, and Kiriath-arba, that [is] Hebron, in [the] hill country of Judah.

en.L: And they set apart Kedesh in Galilee in the hill country of Naphtali, and Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim, and Kiriath-arba, that [is] Hebron, in the hill country of Judah.
en.B: So they set apart these cities: Kedesh in Galilee, in the hill country of Naphtali; Shechem, in the hill country of Ephraim; and Kiriath-arba, which is Hebron, in the hill country of Judah.
en.R: So the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} set apart three towns west of the Jordan River: Kedesh in Galilee, in the hills of Naphtali; Shechem, in the hills of Ephraim; and Kiriath-arba, also called Hebron, in the hills of Judah.

sw.L: Nao wakatenga Kedeshi katika Galilaya katika nchi ya milima ya Naftali, na Shekemu katika nchi ya milima ya Efraimu, na Kiriath-arba, yaani Hebroni, katika nchi ya milima ya Yuda.
sw.B: Basi walitenga miji hii: Kedeshi katika Galilaya, katika nchi ya milima ya Naftali; Shekemu, katika nchi ya milima ya Efraimu; na Kiriath-arba, yaani Hebroni, katika nchi ya milima ya Yuda.
sw.R: Basi Waisraeli walitenga miji mitatu upande wa magharibi wa Mto Yordani: Kedeshi katika Galilaya, katika milima ya Naftali; Shekemu, katika milima ya Efraimu; na Kiriath-arba, ambao pia huitwa Hebroni, katika milima ya Yuda.

es.L: Y apartaron Cedes en Galilea, en la región montañosa de Neftalí, y Siquem en la región montañosa de Efraín, y Quiriat-arbá, que [es] Hebrón, en la región montañosa de Judá.
es.B: Apartaron, pues, estas ciudades: Cedes en Galilea, en la región montañosa de Neftalí; Siquem, en la región montañosa de Efraín; y Quiriat-arbá, que es Hebrón, en la región montañosa de Judá.
es.R: Así que los israelitas apartaron tres pueblos al oeste del río Jordán: Cedes en Galilea, en las montañas de Neftalí; Siquem, en las montañas de Efraín; y Quiriat-arbá, que también se llama Hebrón, en las montañas de Judá.

fr.L: Et ils consacrèrent Kédesh en Galilée, dans la montagne de Nephtali, et Sichem dans la montagne d’Éphraïm, et Kiryath-Arba, c’[est] Hébron, dans la montagne de Juda.
fr.B: Ils consacrèrent donc ces villes : Kédesh en Galilée, dans la région montagneuse de Nephtali ; Sichem, dans la région montagneuse d’Éphraïm ; et Kiryath-Arba, c’est-à-dire Hébron, dans la région montagneuse de Juda.
fr.R: Les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} ont donc mis à part trois villes à l’ouest du Jourdain : Kédesh en Galilée, dans les montagnes de Nephtali ; Sichem, dans les montagnes d’Éphraïm ; et Kiryath-Arba, qu’on appelle aussi Hébron, dans les montagnes de Juda.

vi.L: Họ biệt riêng Kê-đe ở Ga-li-lê trong miền núi Nép-ta-li, Si-chem trong miền núi Ép-ra-im, và Ki-ri-át A-ra-ba, tức là Hếp-rôn, trong miền núi Giu-đa.
vi.B: Vậy họ biệt riêng các thành sau: Kê-đe ở Ga-li-lê, trong miền núi Nép-ta-li; Si-chem, trong miền núi Ép-ra-im; và Ki-ri-át A-ra-ba, tức là Hếp-rôn, trong miền núi Giu-đa.
vi.R: Vậy dân Y-sơ-ra-ên biệt riêng ba thành ở phía tây sông Giô-đanh: Kê-đe ở Ga-li-lê, trong vùng đồi núi Nép-ta-li; Si-chem, trong vùng đồi núi Ép-ra-im; và Ki-ri-át A-ra-ba, cũng gọi là Hếp-rôn, trong vùng đồi núi Giu-đa.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 납달리 산지에 있는 갈릴리의 게데스와 에브라임 산지에 있는 세겜과 유다 산지에 있는 기럇 아르바, 곧 헤브론을 구별하였다.
ko.B: 그래서 그들은 이 성읍들을 구별하여 정하였다. 납달리 산지에 있는 갈릴리의 게데스와 에브라임 산지에 있는 세겜과 유다 산지에 있는 기럇 아르바, 곧 헤브론이다.
ko.R: 그래서 이스라엘 백성은 요단강 서쪽에서 세 성읍을 따로 정하였다. 납달리 산지에 있는 갈릴리의 게데스와 에브라임 산지에 있는 세겜과 유다 산지에 있는 기럇 아르바, 곧 헤브론이다.

decisions.choice: set apart: dedicate to a sacred purpose
decisions.reason: The verb is the one for making something holy. The towns were set aside by God's command for a special use, as places of protection.

decisions.choice: Kedesh, Shechem, Hebron: one town in the north, one in the center, one in the south
decisions.reason: The three towns lie in the northern, central and southern hill country west of the Jordan, so that each part of the land had a refuge within reach (Deuteronomy 19:3).

decisions.choice: Kiriath-arba, that is Hebron: the older name and the later one
decisions.reason: Kiriath-arba was the earlier name of Hebron (14:15; 15:13; Genesis 23:2).

decisions.choice: these cities: (Balanced) / the Israelites ... three towns west of the Jordan River (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced introduces the list with "these cities". Readable also names who set the towns apart and adds that these three were west of the Jordan, to set them beside the three east of it in verse 8.

source.text: וּמֵעֵ֜בֶר לְיַרְדֵּ֤ן יְרִיחוֹ֙ מִזְרָ֔חָה נָתְנ֞וּ אֶת־בֶּ֧צֶר בַּמִּדְבָּ֛ר בַּמִּישֹׁ֖ר מִמַּטֵּ֣ה רְאוּבֵ֑ן וְאֶת־רָאמֹ֤ת בַּגִּלְעָד֙ מִמַּטֵּה־גָ֔ד וְאֶת־גּוֹלָ֥ן בַּבָּשָׁ֖ן מִמַּטֵּ֥ה מְנַשֶּֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: And from [the] other side of [the] Jordan [of] Jericho eastward they gave Bezer in the wilderness on the plateau from [the] tribe of Reuben, and Ramoth in Gilead from [the] tribe of Gad, and Golan in Bashan from [the] tribe of Manasseh.

en.L: And across the Jordan [at] Jericho, eastward, they assigned Bezer in the wilderness on the plateau, from the tribe of Reuben, and Ramoth in Gilead, from the tribe of Gad, and Golan in Bashan, from the tribe of Manasseh.
en.B: East of the Jordan, across from Jericho, they assigned Bezer in the wilderness on the plateau, from the tribe of Reuben; Ramoth in Gilead, from the tribe of Gad; and Golan in Bashan, from the tribe of Manasseh.
en.R: On the east side of the Jordan River, across from Jericho, they chose Bezer in the desert on the high plain, from the tribe of Reuben; Ramoth in Gilead, from the tribe of Gad; and Golan in Bashan, from the tribe of Manasseh.

sw.L: Na ng'ambo ya Yordani [karibu na] Yeriko, upande wa mashariki, wakaweka Beseri nyikani katika uwanda wa juu, kutoka kabila la Reubeni, na Ramothi katika Gileadi, kutoka kabila la Gadi, na Golani katika Bashani, kutoka kabila la Manase.
sw.B: Upande wa mashariki wa Yordani, mkabala na Yeriko, waliweka Beseri nyikani katika uwanda wa juu, kutoka kabila la Reubeni; Ramothi katika Gileadi, kutoka kabila la Gadi; na Golani katika Bashani, kutoka kabila la Manase.
sw.R: Upande wa mashariki wa Mto Yordani, mkabala na Yeriko, walichagua Beseri katika jangwa la nchi tambarare ya juu, kutoka kabila la Reubeni; Ramothi katika Gileadi, kutoka kabila la Gadi; na Golani katika Bashani, kutoka kabila la Manase.

es.L: Y al otro lado del Jordán de Jericó, al oriente, señalaron Béser en el desierto, en la meseta, de la tribu de Rubén, y Ramot en Galaad, de la tribu de Gad, y Golán en Basán, de la tribu de Manasés.
es.B: Al este del Jordán, frente a Jericó, señalaron Béser, en el desierto, en la meseta, de la tribu de Rubén; Ramot de Galaad, de la tribu de Gad; y Golán de Basán, de la tribu de Manasés.
es.R: Al lado este del río Jordán, frente a Jericó, escogieron Béser, en el desierto de la llanura alta, de la tribu de Rubén; Ramot, en Galaad, de la tribu de Gad; y Golán, en Basán, de la tribu de Manasés.

fr.L: Et au-delà du Jourdain de Jéricho, vers l’orient, ils désignèrent Betser dans le désert, sur le plateau, de la tribu de Ruben, et Ramoth en Galaad, de la tribu de Gad, et Golân dans le Bashân, de la tribu de Manassé.
fr.B: À l’est du Jourdain, en face de Jéricho, ils désignèrent Betser, dans le désert, sur le plateau, dans la tribu de Ruben ; Ramoth en Galaad, dans la tribu de Gad ; et Golân dans le Bashân, dans la tribu de Manassé.
fr.R: À l’est du Jourdain, en face de Jéricho, ils ont choisi Betser, dans le désert, sur le haut plateau, dans la tribu de Ruben ; Ramoth en Galaad, dans la tribu de Gad ; et Golân dans le Bashân, dans la tribu de Manassé.

vi.L: Bên kia sông Giô-đanh [tại] Giê-ri-cô, về phía đông, họ định Bê-xe trong đồng hoang trên cao nguyên, từ chi tộc Ru-bên, Ra-mốt ở Ga-la-át, từ chi tộc Gát, và Gô-lan ở Ba-san, từ chi tộc Ma-na-se.
vi.B: Ở phía đông sông Giô-đanh, đối diện Giê-ri-cô, họ chỉ định Bê-xe trong đồng hoang trên cao nguyên, từ chi tộc Ru-bên; Ra-mốt ở Ga-la-át, từ chi tộc Gát; và Gô-lan ở Ba-san, từ chi tộc Ma-na-se.
vi.R: Ở phía đông sông Giô-đanh, đối diện Giê-ri-cô, họ chọn Bê-xe trong hoang mạc trên cao nguyên, từ chi tộc Ru-bên; Ra-mốt ở Ga-la-át, từ chi tộc Gát; và Gô-lan ở Ba-san, từ chi tộc Ma-na-se.

ko.L: 그리고 여리고 요단 건너편 동쪽에서는 르우벤 지파 중에서 평원 광야에 있는 베셀과, 갓 지파 중에서 길르앗에 있는 라못과, 므낫세 지파 중에서 바산에 있는 골란을 정하였다.
ko.B: 요단강 동쪽, 여리고 맞은편에서는 르우벤 지파에서 평원 광야에 있는 베셀을, 갓 지파에서 길르앗에 있는 라못을, 므낫세 지파에서 바산에 있는 골란을 정하였다.
ko.R: 요단강 동쪽, 여리고 맞은편에서는 르우벤 지파의 땅에서 높은 평원의 광야에 있는 베셀을 골랐다. 갓 지파의 땅에서는 길르앗에 있는 라못을, 므낫세 지파의 땅에서는 바산에 있는 골란을 골랐다.

decisions.choice: Bezer, Ramoth, Golan: the three eastern cities Moses had named
decisions.reason: Moses had already set these three cities apart east of the Jordan (Deuteronomy 4:41-43). Here they are formally given as cities of refuge, from south to north.

decisions.choice: across the Jordan of Jericho: the stretch of the Jordan near Jericho
decisions.reason: "The Jordan of Jericho" names the part of the river opposite Jericho, as in Numbers 22:1. "Across" is said from the land west of the river, and "eastward" makes plain that the east side is meant.

decisions.choice: the plateau: the high tableland north of the Arnon
decisions.reason: The word means level ground. It names the high plain east of the Dead Sea (13:9, 16; Deuteronomy 4:43).

decisions.choice: Golan: the name as read in the margin of the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Hebrew manuscript writes the name with slightly different letters and notes in the margin how it is to be read. The difference is only one of spelling; both point to Golan (Deuteronomy 4:43; Joshua 21:27).

decisions.choice: the desert on the high plain
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words for "wilderness" and "plateau", as in Deuteronomy 4:43.

source.text: אֵ֣לֶּה הָיוּ֩ עָרֵ֨י הַמּֽוּעָדָ֜ה לְכֹ֣ל׀בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וְלַגֵּר֙ הַגָּ֣ר בְּתוֹכָ֔ם לָנ֣וּס שָׁ֔מָּה כָּל־מַכֵּה־נֶ֖פֶשׁ בִּשְׁגָגָ֑ה וְלֹ֣א יָמ֗וּת בְּיַד֙ גֹּאֵ֣ל הַדָּ֔ם עַד־עָמְד֖וֹ לִפְנֵ֥י הָעֵדָֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: These were [the] cities of the appointment for all [the] sons of Israel and for the sojourner sojourning among them, to flee there any striking [a] person by inadvertence, and not he will die by [the] hand of [the] avenger of the blood until his standing before the congregation.

en.L: These were the appointed cities for all the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel and for the sojourner who sojourns among them, for anyone who strikes a person by mistake to flee there, so that he may not die by the hand of the avenger of blood until he stands before the congregation.
en.B: These were the cities designated for all the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and for the outsiders living among them. Anyone who killed a person by mistake could flee there and not die at the hands of the avenger of blood before standing trial before the congregation.
en.R: These were the towns chosen for all the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and for the outsiders who lived among them. Anyone who killed a person by accident could run away to one of them. Then the relative who avenges the death could not kill {{gender:them|him}} before the community had judged the case.

sw.L: Hii ndiyo iliyokuwa miji iliyowekwa kwa ajili ya wana wote wa Israeli na kwa ajili ya mgeni akaaye kati yao, ili yeyote amwuaye mtu kwa makosa akimbilie huko, asije akafa kwa mkono wa mlipiza kisasi wa damu mpaka atakaposimama mbele ya jumuiya.
sw.B: Hii ndiyo iliyokuwa miji iliyowekwa kwa ajili ya Waisraeli wote na kwa ajili ya wageni wanaoishi kati yao. Yeyote aliyemwua mtu kwa makosa angeweza kukimbilia huko, asife kwa mkono wa mlipiza kisasi wa damu kabla ya kusimama mbele ya jumuiya kuhukumiwa.
sw.R: Hii ndiyo iliyokuwa miji iliyochaguliwa kwa ajili ya Waisraeli wote na kwa ajili ya wageni walioishi kati yao. Yeyote aliyemwua mtu kwa bahati mbaya angeweza kukimbilia mmojawapo wa miji hiyo. Hivyo ndugu anayelipiza kisasi cha kifo asingeweza kumwua kabla jumuiya haijalihukumu shauri lake.

es.L: Estas fueron las ciudades señaladas para todos los hijos de Israel y para el extranjero que habita entre ellos, para que huyera allí cualquiera que hiriera a una persona por error, y no muriera a mano del vengador de la sangre hasta que compareciera ante la comunidad.
es.B: Estas fueron las ciudades designadas para todos los israelitas y para los extranjeros que vivían entre ellos. Cualquiera que matara a una persona por error podía huir allí y no morir a manos del vengador de la sangre antes de comparecer en juicio ante la comunidad.
es.R: Estos fueron los pueblos escogidos para todos los israelitas y para los extranjeros que vivían entre ellos. Cualquiera que matara a una persona por accidente podía huir a uno de ellos. Así el pariente que venga la muerte no podía matar a esa persona antes de que la comunidad juzgara el caso.

fr.L: Telles furent les villes désignées pour tous les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël et pour l’immigré qui séjourne au milieu d’eux, pour que s’y enfuie quiconque frappe une personne par erreur, et qu’il ne meure pas de la main du vengeur du sang avant d’avoir comparu devant la communauté.
fr.B: Telles furent les villes désignées pour tous les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} et pour les étrangers qui vivaient au milieu d’eux. Quiconque avait tué une personne par erreur pouvait s’y réfugier et ne pas mourir de la main du vengeur du sang avant d’avoir comparu en jugement devant la communauté.
fr.R: Ce sont les villes choisies pour tous les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} et pour les étrangers qui vivaient au milieu d’eux. Celui qui avait tué quelqu’un par accident pouvait s’enfuir dans l’une d’elles. Alors le parent qui venge le mort ne pouvait pas le tuer avant que la communauté ait jugé son cas.

vi.L: Đó là các thành được chỉ định cho toàn thể con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên và cho khách kiều ngụ giữa họ, để bất cứ ai lỡ tay đánh chết một người có thể trốn đến đó, hầu khỏi chết bởi tay người báo thù máu cho đến khi đứng trước hội chúng.
vi.B: Đó là các thành được chỉ định cho toàn dân Y-sơ-ra-ên và cho người ngoại kiều sống giữa họ. Ai lỡ tay giết người có thể trốn đến đó và không bị chết bởi tay người báo thù máu trước khi ra hầu tòa trước hội chúng.
vi.R: Đó là các thành được chọn cho toàn dân Y-sơ-ra-ên và cho người nước ngoài sống giữa họ. Ai vô tình giết người có thể chạy trốn đến một trong các thành ấy. Khi đó người bà con muốn báo thù không thể giết người ấy trước khi cộng đồng xét xử vụ việc.

ko.L: 이것들은 모든 이스라엘 자손과 그들 가운데 머물러 사는 나그네를 위하여 정한 성읍들이니, 누구든지 실수로 사람을 친 자가 그리로 도망하여, 회중 앞에 설 때까지 피의 보복자의 손에 죽지 않게 하려는 것이다.
ko.B: 이것이 모든 이스라엘 자손과 그들 가운데 머물러 사는 나그네를 위하여 정한 성읍들이다. 누구든지 실수로 사람을 죽인 사람은 그리로 도망하여, 회중 앞에서 재판을 받기 전에 피의 보복자의 손에 죽지 않게 하였다.
ko.R: 이것이 모든 이스라엘 백성과 그들 가운데 함께 사는 나그네를 위하여 정한 성읍들이다. 누구든지 실수로 사람을 죽인 사람은 이 성읍들 가운데 하나로 도망할 수 있었다. 그러면 공동체가 그 일을 재판하기 전에는 죽은 사람의 원수를 갚으려는 친척이 그 사람을 죽일 수 없었다.

decisions.choice: cities of the appointment: the designated cities
decisions.reason: The word for appointment is found only here. It comes from a verb meaning to fix or appoint, so the phrase means cities chosen and set for this purpose.

decisions.choice: the sojourner among them: an outsider living in Israel also had the right of refuge
decisions.reason: A sojourner was someone from outside Israel who lived among the people without family land. The law of refuge protected such a person just as it protected an Israelite (Numbers 35:15).

decisions.choice: until he stands before the congregation: the protection lasts until the trial
decisions.reason: The city kept the avenger from killing the person before the congregation had heard the case, as in verse 6 and Numbers 35:12.

decisions.choice: sojourner (Literal) / outsiders (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The same words as in Leviticus and Numbers for a resident from outside Israel; "foreigner" is kept for another Hebrew word.

decisions.choice: "el extranjero" (L); "los extranjeros" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the Pentateuch terms list sets for the ger, the outsider who lives among Israel without belonging to its tribes. The law of refuge protects him as it protects the Israelite (Numbers 35:15).

decisions.choice: "l'immigré" (L), "les étrangers" (B, R) for the ger
decisions.reason: The Pentateuch note sets "l'étranger, l'immigré" for the ger, the outsider who lives in Israel. Literal uses "immigré", which keeps the sense of one who has come to stay; Balanced and Readable use the everyday "étrangers".

decisions.choice: "나그네" for the sojourner at every level
decisions.reason: The *ger* is an outsider who lives among Israel without belonging to a tribe (meaning decision m2). "나그네" is the word Korean has long used for him; "외국인" is kept for the true foreigner, as the English keeps "foreigner".
